o: A separate KYC for each AMC
A one-time KYC valid across all SEBI intermediaries
e: CKYC is a centralised one-time KYC. Once completed with any SEBI-registered intermediary, the same record is reused across all of them. Investors don't need to redo KYC for each new AMC.

q: Up to how many nominees can be registered per mutual fund folio?
e: Up to 3 nominees can be registered per folio, with percentages summing to 100%. Nomination is mandatory; if the investor doesn't nominate, an explicit opt-out must be signed.

q: For a non-liquid open-ended scheme, the redemption cut-off time is:
e: Redemption cut-off for non-liquid schemes is 3:00 PM. Liquid funds use 1:30 PM for subscription but 3:00 PM for redemption.

q: Equity MF redemption proceeds are typically credited to the investor's bank account within:
e: Equity MF redemption settles in T+2 (two business days post the redemption-applicable NAV date). Liquid funds settle T+1.

q: Liquid MF redemption proceeds are typically credited to the investor's bank account within:
e: Liquid MF redemption settles T+1 — faster than equity (T+2) because the underlying instruments (CPs, T-Bills, MM securities) settle quickly.

q: Required documents for KYC typically include:
o: PAN, address proof, photograph, bank cheque
e: Standard KYC docs: PAN (identity), Aadhaar/Voter ID/DL (address), bank cheque (account), passport-size photo. CKYC bundles these into one record valid across the industry.

o: Enhanced due diligence + senior management approval
e: Per AML/PMLA, PEPs (current/former heads of state, senior politicians, judges, etc.) require Enhanced Due Diligence — additional documentation, source of funds verification, and senior management approval before account opening.

q: Re-KYC frequency for a low-risk investor is typically:
e: Re-KYC schedule: Low risk = 10 years; Medium = 8 years; High risk = 2 years. The classification is based on the AMC's risk assessment of the investor at onboarding.

q: If an MF amount remains unclaimed for more than 3 years, it is paid at:
o: The NAV as of the end of the 3-year period
e: Unclaimed amounts within 3 years → at prevailing NAV. After 3 years → at NAV as of end of the 3-year period (NOT current NAV — otherwise investor would benefit from delay).

q: Which of these is a recognised online platform for cross-AMC mutual fund transactions?
e: MF Utility (MFU) is an industry utility for cross-AMC MF transactions. Other online platforms include CAMS / KFin (RTAs), MF Central, and AMC websites. RBI / SEBI portals are regulator sites, not transaction platforms.

o: A statement from one AMC only
A combined statement of all MF holdings across AMCs, sent monthly
e: CAS is sent monthly via email by AMFI/AMCs, combining holdings across all AMCs that an investor uses (linked to PAN). Replaces the need for multiple AMC-level statements.

q: On the death of the sole holder of a folio, units transfer via:
o: Transmission to nominee or legal heir
e: Transmission moves units from the deceased holder to the nominee (if registered) or the legal heir (with succession certificate / probate). Standard documentation: death certificate, KYC of recipient, indemnity, bank details.

q: An investor's grievance against an AMC, if unresolved internally, is escalated to:
e: Cascade: AMC investor service (30 days) → AMC compliance officer → AMFI → SEBI's SCORES portal → SMARTODR (online dispute resolution). Don't escalate to unrelated regulators.

o: Adding a one-time lump-sum to an existing SIP folio
Auto-increase of SIP installment amount annually (e.g. by 10%)
Switching to a new scheme via SIP
e: Top-up SIP automatically increases the SIP amount annually by a pre-set % (commonly 10%). Helps grow corpus in line with rising income. Different from STP (transfer between schemes).

q: AMCs must allocate at least what % of TER toward investor education?
e: AMCs allocate at least 0.02% of the scheme's TER for investor education and awareness. AMFI's 'Mutual Funds Sahi Hai' campaign is funded from this. Watch for the decimal trap.
